To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
overproduction of the CF transmembrane conductances regulator R domain leads to altered levels of asialylated glycans and increased binding of Pseudomonas by tracheal epithelium.
overexpression of the CFTR regulatory (R) domains in epithelial cell lines results in an increase in asialoGM 1 on the cell surface and an increase in Pseudomonas binding to these cells.
overproduction of the R domain of CFTR leads to increased numbers of asialoglycolipids and increased bacterial binding by epithelial cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie the pathogenesis of cystic fibrosis (CF), a genetic disease that is characterized by abnormal ion transport in the airway and by chronic infection with Pseudomonas.
the role of CFTR in regulating the surface properties of airway epithelial cells.
the role of CFTR in the pathogenesis of cystic fibrosis (CF) lung disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

overproduction of the CF transmembrane conductive regulator (CFTR) regulatory domain leads to increased numbers of asialoganglioside GM1 receptors on the surface of epithelial cells and increased Pseudomona aeruginosa binding and subsequent proinflammatory cytokine release.

overproduction of the CF regulatory domain leads to increased numbers of asialoganglioside GM1 and increased P. aeruginosabinding by epithelial cells, and that these events may be responsible for the increased susceptibility of CF airway epithelial cells to bacterial infection.
CFTR is an important determinant of the surface properties of epithelial cells and that these properties can be altered as a consequence of CFTR dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

overexpression of CFTR's regulatory (R)domain leads to increased asialoGM-1 levels and increased bacterial binding to epithelial cells, and that the increased bacterial binding leads to increased epithelial production of the proinflammatory cytokine, interleukin- 8 (IL-8).

the overexpression of CFTR R domain causes an increase in the levels of asialyloGM1 on epithelial cells, and that this increase is responsible for the increased bacterial adherence and proinflammatory response of the cells with altered CF.

The main takeaway from our work is that
CFTR plays a role in regulating the expression of asialo GM1 on the surface of epithelial cells.
there is a direct correlation between CFTR function and the surface glycolipid content and Pseudomonas binding of epithelial cells.
the CFTR R-domain is important to normal epithelial cell function, and that overproduction of this protein can have deleterious effects on epithelial cells.
